newsitem.title: UK: SCOT MEDIA LIFTS STAKE IN ULSTER TV.
newsitem.headline: SCOT MEDIA LIFTS STAKE IN ULSTER TV.

text.p: Scottish Media Group Plc agreed on Thursday to acquire 13.1 percent of Ulster Television's shares at 205 pence per share. The deal will lift Scottish Media's holding in Ulster to 14.99 percent.
"Scottish Media regards this acquisition as an investment and has no plans to make a takeover offer for Ulster (although it may increase its investment)," the company said in a statement.

Ulster TV stock rose 38.5p to 205p -- some 23 percent -- on Thursday morning. The purchase of 6,892,244 Ulster shares will cost Scottish 14.13 million stg and the company said it intended to pay for it out of its existing facilities and the group's cash resources.
"We have made an investment in Ulster in view of the rapid consolidation and centralisation that is taking place in the ITV system as a whole," said Scottish Media Managing Director Andrew Flanagan.
"The move underlines our common interest in maintaining the presence of strong players who value quality regional programming and identity," he added.
Ulster operates the ITV (commercial terrestrial TV) licence for Northern Ireland. It had 1996 pre-tax profits of 8.2 million stg.

Scottish Media, formerly known as Scottish Television, has recently strengthened its grip on ITV north of the border, acquiring Grampian Television to add to its existing licence for the densely populated central Scotland region.
It expanded beyond its original TV base last year when it acquired leading Glasgow newspapers the Herald and Evening Times for 120 million stg.

The lifting of the two-licence ownership cap for ITV companies has seen a wave of consolidation. Carlton Communications Plc, Granada Group Plc and United News & Media have emerged as the dominant players in England and Wales.
